chapter.en: PART I PRELIMINARY

heading.en: Citation and commencement

text.en: 1. These Regulations may be cited as the Casino Control (Gaming Equipment) Regulations 2009 and shall come into operation on 9th September 2009.

chapter.en: PART I PRELIMINARY

heading.en: Definitions

chapter.en: PART II GAMING MACHINES AND GAMING PROGRAMS

heading.en: Application to be approved manufacturer

text.en:
3.—(1) For the purposes of section 103A(1)(a) of the Act, any manufacturer of gaming machines or gaming programs that intends to manufacture gaming machines or gaming programs for use in any casino may apply to the Authority to be an approved manufacturer.
[S 641/2026 wef 21/09/2026]
(2) A consolidated application may be submitted on behalf of a group of corporations, consisting of related corporations within the meaning of section 6 of the Companies Act 1967, for each corporation named in the application (each considered an applicant for the purpose of this Part) to be approved as an approved manufacturer.
[S 643/2022 wef 31/12/2021]
[S 641/2026 wef 21/09/2026]
(3) Every application under paragraph (1) or (2) shall be submitted in such form and manner as the Authority may provide and shall be accompanied by —
(a)the appropriate application fee specified in the First Schedule, which fee is not refundable;
(b)the disclosure of corporate or individual information in the form provided by the Authority for the applicant or each applicant (in the case of a consolidated application) and such associates of the applicant or applicants as the Authority may specify;
[S 641/2026 wef 21/09/2026]
(ba)the disclosure of information in the form provided by the Authority on any manufacturing facility or supplier of the applicant; and
[S 641/2026 wef 21/09/2026]
(c)any other document or information that the Authority may require to determine the application.
[S 641/2026 wef 21/09/2026]
(4) The Authority shall, on receiving an application under paragraph (1) or (2), cause to be carried out all such investigations and inquiries in relation to the applicant or each applicant (in the case of a consolidated application) as it considers necessary to enable it to consider the application properly and, in particular, may —
(a)investigate any of the following persons in relation to the applicant’s suitability to be an approved manufacturer:
(i)the applicant;
(ii)any associate, business associate or supplier of the applicant;
(iii)the manager of any manufacturing facility of the applicant;
(iv)any other person whose association with the applicant is, in the opinion of the Authority, relevant to the application;
[S 641/2026 wef 21/09/2026]
(b)require any person mentioned in sub-paragraph (a) to —
(i)provide any information, or produce any record, relevant to the investigation of the application as may be necessary and in the manner that the Authority may require; or
(ii)furnish any authorisation or consent that the Authority may direct for the purpose of enabling the Authority to obtain information (including financial and other confidential information) concerning the applicant, associate, business associate, supplier, manager or other person (as the case may be) from other persons;
[S 641/2026 wef 21/09/2026]
(c)require the applicant to allow the Authority, its officer or its agent to inspect —
(i)any premises in Singapore or elsewhere where the applicant carries on business; or
(ii)any manufacturing facility of the applicant in Singapore or elsewhere that is owned or occupied by the applicant; or
[S 641/2026 wef 21/09/2026]
(d)require the applicant to take reasonable steps to enable the Authority, its officer or its agent to inspect any manufacturing facility of the applicant in Singapore or elsewhere that is not owned or occupied by the applicant.
[S 641/2026 wef 21/09/2026]
(4A) The Authority, its officer or its agent is not liable to pay any person any fee, charge or expense on account of any inspection under paragraph (4)(c) or (d).
[S 641/2026 wef 21/09/2026]
(5) The Authority may refuse to consider an application under paragraph (1) or (2) if ––
(a)the application is incomplete;
(b)any person refuses to allow the investigation or fails to comply with any requirement of the Authority under paragraph (4) in respect of that application; or
(c)the application fee or the estimated costs of investigation required under regulation 26A(2) are not paid.
[S 64/2013 wef 31/01/2013]
[S 641/2026 wef 21/09/2026]

heading.en: Determination of application

text.en:
5.—(1) The Authority may, if it is satisfied that an applicant is suitable to be an approved manufacturer, by issuing a letter to the applicant, approve the applicant to be an approved manufacturer, subject to any condition that the Authority may impose.
(2) For the purposes of determining whether an applicant is suitable to be an approved manufacturer, the Authority may have regard (but is not limited) to any matter in the Fourth Schedule as it applies to any person mentioned in regulation 3(4)(a).
[S 641/2026 wef 21/09/2026]

chapter.en: PART II GAMING MACHINES AND GAMING PROGRAMS

heading.en: List of approved manufacturers and authorised suppliers

text.en:
6. The Authority may maintain a list of approved manufacturers and authorised suppliers and publish the list on its official website.
[S 641/2026 wef 21/09/2026]

chapter.en: PART II GAMING MACHINES AND GAMING PROGRAMS

heading.en: Duties of approved manufacturer

text.en:
7.—(1) Every approved manufacturer shall comply with the following duties:
(a)notify the Authority in writing of any of the matters set out in the Second Schedule, as soon as practicable and, in any event, no later than 14 days after becoming aware that the event has occurred or such longer period as the Authority may allow in any particular case;
[S 641/2026 wef 21/09/2026]
(b)when requested by the Authority to do so —
(i)provide to the Authority such information as the Authority may specify;
[S 64/2013 wef 31/01/2013]
(ii)produce such records as the Authority may specify and permit the Authority to examine the records, take extracts from them and make copies of them; and
(iii)furnish such authorisation or consent as the Authority may direct for the purpose of enabling the Authority to obtain information (including financial and any confidential information) concerning the approved manufacturer or any associate of the approved manufacturer from any other person; and
[S 64/2013 wef 31/01/2013]
[S 641/2026 wef 21/09/2026]
(c)attend before the Authority or an inspector in relation to any matters relevant to its approval as an approved manufacturer, or to other matters specified by the Authority, and to answer questions relating to those matters.
[S 641/2026 wef 21/09/2026]
[S 641/2026 wef 21/09/2026]
(2) Every approved manufacturer shall, in addition, comply with the following requirements:
(a)ensure that every gaming machine or gaming program manufactured for any casino ––
(i)has been manufactured to comply with the technical standards applicable to that gaming machine or gaming program and any other requirements in notices given by the Authority in relation to that gaming machine or gaming program or class of gaming machines or gaming programs; and
[S 641/2026 wef 21/09/2026]
(ii)has been approved by the Authority, or is of a class of gaming machines or gaming programs which has been approved by the Authority;
[S 64/2013 wef 31/01/2013]
[S 641/2026 wef 21/09/2026]
[S 641/2026 wef 21/09/2026]
(ab)provide such written undertaking as may be required by the Authority in furtherance of the objectives of these Regulations;
[S 64/2013 wef 31/01/2013]
(b)ensure that it meets any performance requirements set by the Authority relating to the performance of the gaming machines or gaming programs manufactured for any casino;
[S 64/2013 wef 31/01/2013]
[S 641/2026 wef 21/09/2026]
(c)attend periodic meetings with the Authority when requested to do so;
[S 64/2013 wef 31/01/2013]
(d)where the approved manufacturer has no place of business in Singapore, notify the Authority of an address in Singapore for the service of any document to be served in proceedings in court and a person or persons authorised to accept service on its behalf;
[S 64/2013 wef 31/01/2013]
[S 641/2026 wef 21/09/2026]
(e)allow the Authority, its officer or its agent to inspect, for the purpose of an investigation under regulation 8 —
(i)any premises in Singapore or elsewhere where the approved manufacturer carries on business; or
(ii)any manufacturing facility of the approved manufacturer in Singapore or elsewhere that is owned or occupied by the approved manufacturer;
[S 641/2026 wef 21/09/2026]
(f)take reasonable steps to enable the Authority, its officer or its agent to inspect, for the purpose of an investigation under regulation 8, any manufacturing facility of the approved manufacturer in Singapore or elsewhere that is not owned or occupied by the approved manufacturer;
[S 641/2026 wef 21/09/2026]
(g)when requested to do so by written notice given by the Authority, provide to the Authority, within the period specified in the notice, such information or document in such form and manner requested which —
(i)relates to any matter in the Fourth Schedule as it applies to any person mentioned in regulation 8(1); and
(ii)is relevant to be considered by the Authority for the purposes of a determination mentioned in regulation 8(1) of the approved manufacturer’s suitability to continue as an approved manufacturer.
[S 641/2026 wef 21/09/2026]
[S 641/2026 wef 21/09/2026]
(2A) The Authority, its officer or its agent shall not be liable to pay any person any fee, charge or expense on account of any inspection under paragraph (2)(e) or (f).
[S 64/2013 wef 31/01/2013]
[S 641/2026 wef 21/09/2026]
(3) If any approved manufacturer fails to comply with any of the requirements under this regulation, the Authority may, by written notice, require the approved manufacturer to rectify the failure or take such other corrective action within a specified time as the Authority may determine.
[S 641/2026 wef 21/09/2026]
(4) [Deleted by S 64/2013 wef 31/01/2013]
[S 641/2026 wef 21/09/2026]

chapter.en: PART II GAMING MACHINES AND GAMING PROGRAMS

heading.en: Regular investigation and determination of suitability and technical capability

text.en:
8.—(1) The Authority may, from time to time, investigate ––
(a)an approved manufacturer;
(b)the manager of any manufacturing facility of the approved manufacturer; or
(c)any authorised supplier, associate or business associate of the approved manufacturer,
to determine whether the approved manufacturer is suitable to continue to be an approved manufacturer.
(2) For the purposes of the determination mentioned in paragraph (1), the Authority may have regard (but is not limited) to any matter in the Fourth Schedule as it applies to any person mentioned in that paragraph.
[S 641/2026 wef 21/09/2026]

chapter.en: PART II GAMING MACHINES AND GAMING PROGRAMS

heading.en: Ongoing monitoring of associates and others

text.en:
8A.—(1) The Authority may, from time to time, inquire into ––
(a)the manager of any manufacturing facility of an approved manufacturer;
(b)any authorised supplier, associate or business associate of an approved manufacturer; or
(c)any person likely to become an associate of an approved manufacturer.
[S 641/2026 wef 21/09/2026]
(2) In particular, the Authority must consider whether there is any information relating to any matter in the Fourth Schedule as it applies to any person mentioned in paragraph (1).
[S 641/2026 wef 21/09/2026]
(3) An approved manufacturer shall notify the Authority in writing that a person is likely to become an associate of the approved manufacturer as soon as practicable after the approved manufacturer becomes aware of the likelihood.
[S 641/2026 wef 21/09/2026]
(4) The Authority may, by notice in writing, require a person referred to in paragraph (1) —
(a)to provide the Authority, in accordance with directions in the notice, with such information relevant to the approved manufacturer or the association or business association (as the case may be) of the person with the approved manufacturer, or with such information as the Authority requires, as is specified in the notice;
[S 641/2026 wef 21/09/2026]
(b)to produce to the Authority, in accordance with the directions in the notice, such records relevant to the approved manufacturer or that association or business association, or to matters specified by the Authority, as may be specified in the notice and to permit the Authority to examine the records, take extracts from them and make copies of them; or
[S 641/2026 wef 21/09/2026]
(c)to attend before the Authority for examination in relation to any matter relevant to the approved manufacturer or that association or business association, or to matters specified by the Authority, and to answer questions relating to those matters.
[S 641/2026 wef 21/09/2026]
(5) If records are produced under this regulation, the Authority may retain possession of the records for such period as may reasonably be necessary for inquiries to be carried out.
(6) At any reasonable time during the period for which records are retained, the Authority shall permit inspection of the records by a person who would be entitled to inspect them if they were not in the possession of the Authority.
(7) The Authority may —
(a)require any person mentioned in paragraph (1) who is an individual to consent to having his photograph, finger prints and palm prints taken; and
[S 641/2026 wef 21/09/2026]
(b)send a copy of such photograph, finger prints and palm prints, and any supporting documents to the Commissioner of Police.
(8) The Commissioner of Police or any police officer authorised by the Commissioner shall inquire into and report to the Authority on such matters concerning any person, mentioned in paragraph (1) as the Authority requests.
[S 641/2026 wef 21/09/2026]
(9) If the Authority determines that —
(a)the manager of a manufacturing facility of an approved manufacturer has engaged or is engaging in conduct that, in the opinion of the Authority, is unacceptable for a person who administers or manages a manufacturing facility of the approved manufacturer;
(b)an authorised supplier of an approved manufacturer has engaged or is engaging in conduct that, in the opinion of the Authority, is unacceptable for a person who is supplying gaming machines or gaming programs of the approved manufacturer;
(c)an associate of an approved manufacturer has engaged or is engaging in conduct that, in the opinion of the Authority, is unacceptable for a person who is concerned in or associated with the management or operation of the business of the approved manufacturer; or
(d)a business associate of an approved manufacturer has engaged or is engaging in conduct that, in the opinion of the Authority, is unacceptable for a person who has a business association with the approved manufacturer,
the Authority may give written notice to the manager, authorised supplier, associate or business associate mentioned in sub-paragraph (a), (b), (c) or (d) that the conduct is unacceptable.
[S 641/2026 wef 21/09/2026]
(10) If —
(a)the Authority, having regard to any matter referred to in paragraph (2), determines that —
(i)the manager of a manufacturing facility of an approved manufacturer is unsuitable to be administering or managing a manufacturing facility of the approved manufacturer;
(ii)an authorised supplier of an approved manufacturer is unsuitable to be supplying gaming machines or gaming programs of the approved manufacturer;
(iii)an associate of an approved manufacturer is unsuitable to be concerned in or associated with the management or operation of the business of the approved manufacturer; or
(iv)a business associate of an approved manufacturer is unsuitable to have a business association with the approved manufacturer; or
(b)the manager, authorised supplier, associate or business associate mentioned in paragraph (9)(a), (b), (c) or (d) continues with the conduct mentioned in paragraph (9),
the Authority may, by written notice, direct the approved manufacturer to take all reasonable steps to terminate the association or business association (as the case may be) with the manager, authorised supplier, associate or business associate (as the case may be) and the approved manufacturer must comply with the direction within 14 days after receiving the notice or any longer period agreed with the Authority.
[S 641/2026 wef 21/09/2026]
[S 641/2026 wef 21/09/2026]

chapter.en: PART II GAMING MACHINES AND GAMING PROGRAMS

heading.en: Voluntary discontinuation as approved manufacturer

text.en:
9.—(1) An approved manufacturer may send a request in writing to the Authority to discontinue as an approved manufacturer.
[S 641/2026 wef 21/09/2026]
(2) The Authority may refuse to allow the request under paragraph (1) if ––
(a)any action commenced by the Authority under regulation 10, or any investigation which may result in such action, against the approved manufacturer is pending; or
[S 641/2026 wef 21/09/2026]
(b)any investigation by the Authority in respect of any gaming machine or gaming program manufactured by the approved manufacturer is pending.
[S 641/2026 wef 21/09/2026]
[S 641/2026 wef 21/09/2026]

chapter.en: PART II GAMING MACHINES AND GAMING PROGRAMS

heading.en: Cancellation of approval, etc., in relation to approved manufacturer

text.en:
10.—(1) Where any approved manufacturer —
(a)is, for specified reasons, considered by the Authority to be no longer suitable to continue to be an approved manufacturer;
(aa)fails to comply with any condition imposed by the Authority under regulation 5(1) or 28(1)(c);
[S 641/2026 wef 21/09/2026]
(b)fails to comply with regulation 7(1) or (2) or a written notice under regulation 7(3);
[S 64/2013 wef 31/01/2013]
(c)is convicted of any offence under the Act or regulations made thereunder;
[S 64/2013 wef 31/01/2013]
(d)fails to comply with regulation 8A(3) or (10), 10A or 10B;
[S 64/2013 wef 31/01/2013]
[S 641/2026 wef 21/09/2026]
(e)fails to comply with any written notice of the Authority under regulation 26B(1); or
[S 64/2013 wef 31/01/2013]
[S 641/2026 wef 21/09/2026]
(f)fails to comply with any condition of a waiver imposed by the Authority under regulation 28(1)(b) or 29(4)(b),
[S 641/2026 wef 21/09/2026]
the Authority may take any of the following actions:
(i)issue a letter of censure to the approved manufacturer;
(ii)suspend its approval of the approved manufacturer for a specified period not exceeding 6 months;
(iii)cancel its approval of the approved manufacturer.
[S 641/2026 wef 21/09/2026]
(2) The Authority may, in its discretion, cancel its approval of any approved manufacturer which has had no business dealings with any casino operator for a continuous period of 3 years or more.
[S 641/2026 wef 21/09/2026]
(3) The Authority shall, before taking any action under paragraph (1) or (2), serve on the approved manufacturer a notice in writing giving the person an opportunity to show cause within 14 days, or such longer period as the Authority may allow on application by the approved manufacturer, why action should not be taken under that paragraph.
[S 64/2013 wef 31/01/2013]
[S 641/2026 wef 21/09/2026]
(4) The approved manufacturer may, within the period allowed under paragraph (3), make submissions to the Authority as to why the action should not be taken and the Authority shall consider any submissions so made.
[S 64/2013 wef 31/01/2013]
[S 641/2026 wef 21/09/2026]
(5) The Authority may, if the approved manufacturer fails to show cause within the period allowed under paragraph (3) or fails to show sufficient cause, by giving written notice to the approved manufacturer, take such action in paragraph (1)(i), (ii) or (iii) against that person as the Authority sees fit.
[S 64/2013 wef 31/01/2013]
[S 641/2026 wef 21/09/2026]
(6) The suspension or cancellation of approval under this regulation shall take effect when the notice under paragraph (5) is given or on such later date as may be specified in the notice.
(7) While any approved manufacturer is suspended under this regulation, it shall not, for the purposes of these Regulations, be regarded as an approved manufacturer, as the case may be, during the period of its suspension.
[S 641/2026 wef 21/09/2026]
(8) The Authority may lift the suspension of its approval if it is satisfied that corrective action has been duly taken by the approved manufacturer.
[S 641/2026 wef 21/09/2026]
[S 641/2026 wef 21/09/2026]

chapter.en: PART II GAMING MACHINES AND GAMING PROGRAMS

heading.en: Notification of use of supplier by approved manufacturer

text.en:
10A. For the purposes of section 103A(4)(c) of the Act, every notification under that provision by an approved manufacturer to the Authority must be —
(a)made in the form and manner as the Authority may specify; and
(b)accompanied by any information or document in relation to the supplier that the Authority may require.
[S 641/2026 wef 21/09/2026]

chapter.en: PART II GAMING MACHINES AND GAMING PROGRAMS

heading.en: Notification of cessation of use of authorised supplier

text.en:
10B.—(1) If an approved manufacturer ceases to use an authorised supplier to supply gaming machines or gaming programs of the approved manufacturer, the approved manufacturer must notify the Authority of the cessation within 14 days after the cessation.
(2) The notification mentioned in paragraph (1) must be —
(a)made in the form and manner as the Authority may specify; and
(b)accompanied by any information or document in relation to the cessation that the Authority may require.
[S 641/2026 wef 21/09/2026]

chapter.en: PART II GAMING MACHINES AND GAMING PROGRAMS

heading.en: Definition of “electronic table game”

text.en:
11. For the purposes of the definition of “electronic table game” in section 2(1) of the Act, the following things are prescribed as electronic table games:
(a)any gaming machine or gaming program used to play any casino game that involves the wagering of any money or casino chips (with or without match play coupons) on the outcome of any simulated race, competition or event;
(b)any electronic device through which bets may be placed on the outcome of any simulated race, competition or event.
[S 641/2026 wef 21/09/2026]

chapter.en: PART II GAMING MACHINES AND GAMING PROGRAMS

heading.en: Minimum return to player percentage

text.en:
12.—(1) Subject to paragraph (2), the minimum return to player percentage of each gaming machine or gaming program used in a casino shall be 90%.
[S 641/2026 wef 21/09/2026]
(2) Paragraph (1) shall not apply to any semi-automated electronic table game.
(3) In this regulation, “semi-automated electronic table game” means an electronic table game conducted in a semi-automated manner, where a dealer conducts the game play with the automation of wagering or payment.
[S 64/2013 wef 31/01/2013]

chapter.en: PART II GAMING MACHINES AND GAMING PROGRAMS

heading.en: Gaming machines and gaming programs to comply with technical standards and other requirements

text.en:
13.—(1) Subject to paragraph (3), every gaming machine or gaming program used or intended for use in a casino shall be designed, manufactured, installed, tested, inspected, operated, maintained and repaired in accordance with the technical standards and any other requirements set out in any notice under paragraph (2) relating to the gaming machine or gaming program or class of gaming machines or gaming programs to which it belongs.
[S 641/2026 wef 21/09/2026]
(2) The Authority may from time to time, by notice in writing given to a casino operator or an approved manufacturer, require that any gaming machine or gaming program or class of gaming machines or gaming programs for use in any casino must comply with certain requirements, including but not limited to requirements as to bet limits, game integrity or security.
[S 641/2026 wef 21/09/2026]
(3) The Authority may, on the application of an approved manufacturer or a casino operator, modify or waive any of the technical standards or any other requirements set out in notices under paragraph (2) relating to any gaming machine or gaming program or class of gaming machines or gaming programs, subject to such conditions as the Authority may impose, having regard to bet limits, game integrity or security.
[S 641/2026 wef 21/09/2026]
(4) Without prejudice to paragraph (2), where the technical standards relating to any gaming machine or gaming program or class of gaming machines or gaming programs is revised, the Authority may, by notice in writing in any particular case, require a casino operator to make such modifications to any gaming machine or gaming program or class of gaming machines or gaming programs as may be necessary to comply with any of the revised technical standards.
[S 64/2013 wef 31/01/2013]
[S 641/2026 wef 21/09/2026]
[S 641/2026 wef 21/09/2026]

chapter.en: PART II GAMING MACHINES AND GAMING PROGRAMS

heading.en: Approval of class of gaming machines or gaming programs

text.en:
14.—(1) An application for approval of a class of gaming machines or gaming programs may be made by —
(a)an approved manufacturer; or
[S 641/2026 wef 21/09/2026]
(b)a casino operator (or an applicant for a casino licence) intending to use the gaming machines or gaming programs in any casino.
[S 641/2026 wef 21/09/2026]
[S 641/2026 wef 21/09/2026]
(2) The application under paragraph (1) shall be submitted in such form and manner as the Authority may provide and shall be accompanied by —
(a)the appropriate application fee specified in the First Schedule, which fee is not refundable;
(b)a report issued by an approved test service provider certifying that the class of gaming machines or gaming programs complies with the technical standards or any other requirements set out in notices under regulation 13(2) applicable to it; and
[S 64/2013 wef 31/01/2013]
[S 641/2026 wef 21/09/2026]
(c)any other information or document that the Authority may require to determine the application.
[S 641/2026 wef 21/09/2026]
(3) Where the Authority considers it necessary to conduct any further investigation in relation to any particular application under paragraph (1), the cost of the investigation shall be borne by the person making the application.
(4) The Authority may refuse to consider an application for approval of any class of gaming machines or gaming programs if ––
(a)the application is incomplete;
(b)any person refuses to allow an investigation under paragraph (3), if any, in respect of that application; or
(c)the application fee or the cost of investigation is not paid.
[S 641/2026 wef 21/09/2026]
(5) The Authority may approve the class of gaming machines or gaming programs, subject to such conditions as the Authority may impose.
[S 64/2013 wef 31/01/2013]
[S 641/2026 wef 21/09/2026]
(6) [Deleted by S 64/2013 wef 31/01/2013]
[S 641/2026 wef 21/09/2026]

chapter.en: PART II GAMING MACHINES AND GAMING PROGRAMS

heading.en: Modification of gaming machines or gaming programs

text.en:
15.—(1) No person shall modify, or permit any modification of, any approved class of gaming machines or gaming programs unless the person has obtained the prior written approval of the Authority for the modification.
[S 641/2026 wef 21/09/2026]
(2) Regulation 14(2) to (5) shall apply, with the necessary modifications, to an application for approval under paragraph (1) as it does to an application for approval under regulation 14(1).
(3) The Authority may waive the requirement to apply for approval under paragraph (1) if the Authority is of the opinion that the modification is minor having regard to bet limits, game integrity or security.
(4) Any person other than a casino operator or licensed special employee who contravenes paragraph (1) shall be guilty of an offence and shall be liable on conviction to a fine not exceeding $10,000 or to imprisonment for a term not exceeding 12 months or to both.
[S 641/2026 wef 21/09/2026]
(5) A casino operator which contravenes paragraph (1) shall be liable to disciplinary action under section 54 of the Act.
[S 64/2013 wef 31/01/2013]
(6) A licensed special employee who contravenes paragraph (1) shall be liable to disciplinary action under section 93 of the Act.
[S 641/2026 wef 21/09/2026]
[S 641/2026 wef 21/09/2026]

chapter.en: PART II GAMING MACHINES AND GAMING PROGRAMS

heading.en: Revocation of approval of class of gaming machines or gaming programs

text.en:
16.—(1) Where any approved class of gaming machines or gaming programs or any component of any gaming machine or gaming program of that class —
(a)does not comply with any technical standards or any other requirements in notices given by the Authority applicable to it, or any conditions imposed by the Authority;
(b)has been modified without the prior written approval or waiver of the Authority under regulation 15; or
(c)has failed to function in a manner in which it was designed or programmed to function,
the Authority may, subject to paragraph (2), revoke the approval of the class of gaming machines or gaming programs or the component thereof for use in a casino.
[S 64/2013 wef 31/01/2013]
[S 641/2026 wef 21/09/2026]
(2) The Authority shall not revoke any approval of a class of gaming machines or gaming programs or the component thereof unless the Authority first served on the casino operator a notice in writing giving the casino operator an opportunity to show cause within a specified period why the approval should not be revoked.
[S 64/2013 wef 31/01/2013]
[S 641/2026 wef 21/09/2026]
(3) The Authority may, after considering any submissions made by a casino operator, revoke the approval of the class of gaming machines or gaming programs and give the casino operator written notice thereof.
[S 641/2026 wef 21/09/2026]
(4) Any revocation of approval of a class of gaming machines or gaming programs under this regulation shall take effect when the notice under paragraph (3) is given or on such later date as may be specified in the notice.
[S 641/2026 wef 21/09/2026]
[S 641/2026 wef 21/09/2026]

chapter.en: PART II GAMING MACHINES AND GAMING PROGRAMS

heading.en: Duty of casino operator in relation to gaming machines and gaming programs

text.en:
17.—(1) It shall be the duty of every casino operator to ensure that it does not use or permit to be used in its casino —
(a)any gaming machine or gaming program which does not comply with regulation 12(1) or 13(1);
[S 64/2013 wef 31/01/2013]
[S 641/2026 wef 21/09/2026]
(b)any gaming machine or gaming program which is not of a class approved by the Authority under regulation 14 or the approval of which has been revoked;
[S 641/2026 wef 21/09/2026]
(ba)any gaming machine or gaming program with any component approval of which has been revoked under regulation 16;
[S 64/2013 wef 31/01/2013]
[S 641/2026 wef 21/09/2026]
(c)any gaming machine or gaming program in contravention of any condition of approval under regulation 14(5); or
[S 641/2026 wef 21/09/2026]
(d)any gaming machine or gaming program which has been modified without the prior written approval or waiver of the Authority under regulation 15.
[S 64/2013 wef 31/01/2013]
[S 641/2026 wef 21/09/2026]
(2) A casino operator which contravenes paragraph (1) shall be liable to disciplinary action under section 54 of the Act.
[S 641/2026 wef 21/09/2026]

chapter.en: PART III GAMING EQUIPMENT (OTHER THAN GAMING MACHINES AND GAMING PROGRAMS)

heading.en: Application of this Part

text.en:
18. In this Part, “gaming equipment” does not include gaming machines and gaming programs.
[S 641/2026 wef 21/09/2026]

chapter.en: PART III GAMING EQUIPMENT (OTHER THAN GAMING MACHINES AND GAMING PROGRAMS)

heading.en: Gaming equipment to be approved by Authority

text.en:
19.—(1) Subject to paragraph (2), any gaming equipment used or intended for use in a casino must be ––
(a)approved gaming equipment; and
(b)used in accordance with that approval and any conditions thereof.
(2) The Authority may waive the requirement in paragraph (1) for any gaming equipment or class of gaming equipment.

chapter.en: PART III GAMING EQUIPMENT (OTHER THAN GAMING MACHINES AND GAMING PROGRAMS)

heading.en: Gaming equipment to comply with technical standards and other requirements

text.en:
20.—(1) Subject to paragraph (3), every gaming equipment used or intended for use in a casino shall be designed, manufactured, installed, tested, inspected, operated, maintained and repaired in accordance with the technical standards and any other requirements set out in any notice under paragraph (2) relating to that gaming equipment or class of gaming equipment to which it belongs.
[S 641/2026 wef 21/09/2026]
(2) The Authority may from time to time, by notice in writing given to a casino operator or a manufacturer of gaming equipment, require that any gaming equipment or class of gaming equipment for use in any casino must comply with certain requirements, including but not limited to requirements as to additional testing or reporting to be carried out on the gaming equipment.
[S 641/2026 wef 21/09/2026]
(3) The Authority may, on the application of a manufacturer of the gaming equipment or a casino operator, modify or waive any of the technical standards or requirements in notices under paragraph (2) relating to any gaming equipment or class of gaming equipment, subject to such conditions as the Authority may impose, having regard to bet limits, game integrity or security.
[S 641/2026 wef 21/09/2026]
(4) Without prejudice to paragraph (2), where the technical standards relating to any gaming equipment or class of gaming equipment is revised, the Authority may, by notice in writing in any particular case, require a casino operator to make such modifications to any gaming equipment or class of gaming equipment as may be necessary to comply with any of the revised technical standards.
[S 64/2013 wef 31/01/2013]

chapter.en: PART III GAMING EQUIPMENT (OTHER THAN GAMING MACHINES AND GAMING PROGRAMS)

heading.en: Approved gaming equipment

text.en:
21.—(1) An application for approval of a class of gaming equipment may be made by a casino operator (or an applicant for a casino licence) intending to use, or any manufacturer of gaming equipment intending to manufacture the gaming equipment in any casino.
[S 64/2013 wef 31/01/2013]
[S 641/2026 wef 21/09/2026]
(2) The application under paragraph (1) shall be submitted in such form and manner as the Authority may provide and shall be accompanied by —
(a)the appropriate application fee specified in the First Schedule, which fee is not refundable;
(b)where technical standards or other requirements in notices have been issued under these Regulations in relation to the gaming equipment and have not been waived under regulation 20(3), a report issued by an approved test service provider certifying that the class of gaming equipment complies with those technical standards applicable to it or any other requirements in those notices given by the Authority; and
[S 64/2013 wef 31/01/2013]
(c)any other information or document that the Authority may require to determine the application.
[S 641/2026 wef 21/09/2026]
(3) The Authority may, in addition to any investigation carried out under section 102(1) of the Act, require the manufacturer of the gaming equipment to provide such information or produce such records as may be necessary to determine the application under paragraph (1) and in the manner that the Authority may require.
[S 641/2026 wef 21/09/2026]
(4) The Authority may give a written notice to the applicant under paragraph (1) of the estimated cost of the investigation under section 102(1) of the Act and require the applicant to pay such estimated cost to the Authority within such period as may be specified in the notice.
(5) The Authority may refuse to consider an application for approval of any class of gaming equipment if ––
(a)the application is incomplete;
(b)any person refuses to allow an investigation of the gaming equipment under section 102(1) of the Act or fails to comply with a requirement of the Authority under paragraph (3) in respect of that application; or
(c)the application fee or the estimated cost of investigation required under paragraph (4) is not paid.
(6) At the conclusion of the investigation into the application or if the application is withdrawn, the Authority shall certify the actual cost of the investigation, and shall ––
(a)where the actual cost of investigation is lower than the amount paid under paragraph (4), refund the excess without interest to the person who paid the estimated cost; or
(b)where the actual cost of investigation is higher than the amount paid under paragraph (4), by a written notice, require the applicant to reimburse the Authority the excess within such period as may be specified in the notice.
(7) The Authority may approve the class of gaming equipment, subject to such conditions as the Authority may impose.
[S 64/2013 wef 31/01/2013]

chapter.en: PART III GAMING EQUIPMENT (OTHER THAN GAMING MACHINES AND GAMING PROGRAMS)

heading.en: Modification of approved gaming equipment

text.en:
22.—(1) No person shall modify, or permit any modification of, any approved class of gaming equipment, unless the person has obtained the prior written approval of the Authority for the modification.
(2) Regulation 21(2) to (7) shall apply, with the necessary modifications, to an application for approval under paragraph (1) as it does to an application for approval under regulation 21(1).
(3) The Authority may waive the requirement to apply for approval under paragraph (1) if the Authority is of the opinion that the modification is minor having regard to bet limits, game integrity or security.
(4) Any person other than a casino operator or licensed special employee who contravenes paragraph (1) shall be guilty of an offence and shall be liable on conviction to a fine not exceeding $10,000 or to imprisonment for a term not exceeding 12 months or to both.
[S 641/2026 wef 21/09/2026]
(5) A casino operator which contravenes paragraph (1) shall be liable to disciplinary action under section 54 of the Act.
[S 64/2013 wef 31/01/2013]
(6) A licensed special employee who contravenes paragraph (1) shall be liable to disciplinary action under section 93 of the Act.
[S 641/2026 wef 21/09/2026]

chapter.en: PART III GAMING EQUIPMENT (OTHER THAN GAMING MACHINES AND GAMING PROGRAMS)

heading.en: Regular investigation

text.en:
22A.—(1) The Authority may investigate the manufacturing process of any manufacturer of any approved gaming equipment.
(2) In investigating the manufacturing process under paragraph (1), the Authority shall consider whether ––
(a)the manufacturing process is consistent with the representations made by the manufacturer in any application for approval of gaming equipment under these Regulations; and
(b)the conditions of approval for any class of approved gaming equipment have been complied with by the manufacturer.
(3) The Authority, its officer or its agent may, for the purposes of an investigation under paragraph (1), inspect any premises in Singapore or elsewhere where the manufacturer of approved gaming equipment is carrying on business.
(4) The Authority, its officer or its agent shall not be liable to pay any person any fee, charge or expense on account of any inspection under paragraph (3).
(5) Where any manufacturer of approved gaming equipment, without reasonable excuse, refuses to permit the Authority, its officers or its agents to inspect its premises under paragraph (3), the Authority may revoke the approval of any gaming equipment or any component thereof which is the subject of the inspection.
(6) The Authority may give a written notice to the manufacturer of approved gaming equipment of the estimated cost of the investigation under paragraph (1) and require the manufacturer to pay such estimated cost to the Authority within such period as may be specified in the notice.
(7) At the conclusion of the investigation under paragraph (1), the Authority shall certify the actual cost of the investigation, and shall ––
(a)where the actual cost of investigation is lower than the amount paid under paragraph (6), refund the excess without interest to the manufacturer who paid the estimated cost; or
(b)where the actual cost of investigation is higher than the amount paid under paragraph (6), by a written notice, require the manufacturer to reimburse the Authority the excess within such period as may be specified in the notice.
(8) In this regulation, “manufacturing process” includes the following processes and procedures relating to the manufacture of gaming equipment:
(a)the procurement of any materials, services, machinery or equipment in connection with the manufacture of gaming equipment;
(b)the design, manufacture, modification, repair or testing of gaming equipment;
(c)measures relating to the quality control of gaming equipment; or
(d)the storage or delivery of gaming equipment intended for use in any casino, including any security measures for such storage or delivery.
[S 64/2013 wef 31/01/2013]

chapter.en: PART III GAMING EQUIPMENT (OTHER THAN GAMING MACHINES AND GAMING PROGRAMS)

heading.en: Revocation of approval of class of gaming equipment

text.en:
23.—(1) Where any approved class of gaming equipment or any component of any gaming equipment of that class —
(a)does not comply with any technical standards or any other requirements in notices given by the Authority applicable to it, or any conditions imposed by the Authority;
(b)has been modified without the prior written approval or waiver of the Authority under regulation 22; or
(c)has failed to function in a manner in which it was designed or programmed to function,
the Authority may, subject to paragraph (2), revoke the approval of the class of gaming equipment or the component thereof for use in a casino.
[S 64/2013 wef 31/01/2013]
(2) The Authority shall not revoke any approval of a class of gaming equipment or the component thereof unless the Authority first served on the casino operator a notice in writing giving the casino operator an opportunity to show cause within a specified period why the approval should not be revoked.
[S 64/2013 wef 31/01/2013]
(3) The Authority may, after considering any submissions made by a casino operator, revoke the approval of the class of gaming equipment and give the casino operator written notice thereof.
(4) Any revocation of approval of a class of gaming equipment under this regulation shall take effect when the notice under paragraph (3) is given or on such later date as may be specified in the notice.

chapter.en: PART III GAMING EQUIPMENT (OTHER THAN GAMING MACHINES AND GAMING PROGRAMS)

heading.en: Duty of casino operator in relation to gaming equipment

text.en:
24.—(1) It shall be the duty of every casino operator to ensure that it does not use or permit to be used in its casino —
(a)any gaming equipment which is not of a class approved by the Authority under regulation 21 or the approval of which has been revoked (unless the requirement for approval is waived under regulation 19(2));
(aa)any gaming equipment with any component approval of which has been revoked by the Authority under regulation 23;
[S 64/2013 wef 31/01/2013]
[S 641/2026 wef 21/09/2026]
(b)any approved gaming equipment other than in accordance with any conditions of such approval under regulation 21(7);
(c)any gaming equipment not designed, manufactured, installed, tested, operated, maintained or repaired in accordance with regulation 20(1); or
[S 641/2026 wef 21/09/2026]
(d)any approved gaming equipment which has been modified without the prior written approval or waiver of the Authority under regulation 22.
[S 64/2013 wef 31/01/2013]
(2) A casino operator which contravenes paragraph (1) shall be liable to disciplinary action under section 54 of the Act.

chapter.en: PART IIIA TESTING SERVICES

heading.en: Application to be approved test service provider

text.en:
24A.—(1) For the purposes of section 103A(1)(b) of the Act, any person intending to supply any testing services in relation to any gaming equipment for use in any casino may apply to the Authority to be an approved test service provider in such form as the Authority may, from time to time provide, which must be accompanied by —
(a)the appropriate application fee as specified in the First Schedule, which fee is not refundable;
(b)the disclosure of corporate or individual information in the form as provided by the Authority relating to the applicant and such associate of the applicant as the Authority may specify;
(c)information on every test facility at which the applicant proposes to test gaming equipment for use in any casino;
(d)a written statement from the applicant, in such form as the Authority may require, attesting to the impartiality and independence from direction and control of any person in the gaming equipment industry in Singapore or elsewhere of the applicant, its associates and its employees; and
(e)any other information or document that the Authority may require to determine the application.
[S 641/2026 wef 21/09/2026]
[S 641/2026 wef 21/09/2026]
(2) The Authority shall, on receiving an application under paragraph (1), cause to be carried out all such investigations and inquiries in relation to the applicant as it considers necessary to enable it to consider the application properly and, in particular, may —
(a)investigate any of the following persons in relation to the applicant’s suitability to be an approved test service provider:
(i)the applicant;
(ii)any associate or business associate of the applicant;
(iii)any other person whose association with the applicant is, in the opinion of the Authority, relevant to the application;
[S 641/2026 wef 21/09/2026]
(b)require the person mentioned in sub-paragraph (a) to —
(i)provide any information, or produce any record, relevant to the investigation of the application as may be necessary and in the manner that the Authority may require; or
(ii)furnish any authorisation or consent that the Authority may direct for the purpose of enabling the Authority to obtain information (including financial and other confidential information) concerning the applicant, associate, business associate or other person (as the case may be) from other persons; and
[S 641/2026 wef 21/09/2026]
(c)require the applicant to allow the Authority, its officer or its agent to inspect any premises in Singapore or elsewhere where the applicant carries on business, including the test facilities of the applicant.
[S 641/2026 wef 21/09/2026]
(2A) The Authority, its officer or its agent is not liable to pay any person any fee, charge or expense on account of any inspection under paragraph (2)(c).
[S 641/2026 wef 21/09/2026]
(3) The Authority may refuse to consider an application under paragraph (1) if ––
(a)the application is incomplete;
(b)any person refuses to allow the investigation or fails to comply with any requirement of the Authority under paragraph (2) in respect of that application; or
(c)the application fee or the estimated costs of investigation required under regulation 26A(2) are not paid.
[S 64/2013 wef 31/01/2013]

chapter.en: PART IIIA TESTING SERVICES

heading.en: Determination of application

text.en:
24B.—(1) The Authority may, if it is satisfied that an applicant is suitable to be an approved test service provider, by issuing a letter to the applicant, approve the applicant to be an approved test service provider, subject to any condition that the Authority may impose (including conditions designating any test facilities where testing services can be carried out).
(2) For the purposes of determining whether an applicant is suitable to be an approved test service provider, the Authority may have regard (but is not limited) to any matter in the Fourth Schedule as it applies to any person mentioned in regulation 24A(2)(a).
[S 641/2026 wef 21/09/2026]

chapter.en: PART IIIA TESTING SERVICES

heading.en: List of approved test service providers

text.en:
24C. The Authority may maintain a list of approved test service providers and publish the list on its official website.
[S 641/2026 wef 21/09/2026]

chapter.en: PART IIIA TESTING SERVICES

heading.en: Duties of approved test service provider

chapter.en: PART IIIA TESTING SERVICES

heading.en: Approved test service provider to comply with codes, etc., and other requirements

text.en:
24E.—(1) Subject to paragraph (3), all approved test service providers shall comply with the codes, standards of performance or specifications issued or approved by the Authority under section 200B of the Act which relate to testing services in relation to any gaming equipment and any other requirements set out in notices under paragraph (2).
[S 641/2026 wef 21/09/2026]
(2) The Authority may, from time to time, by notice in writing given to an approved test service provider, require that any approved test service provider must comply with certain requirements, including but not limited to requirements as to the integrity of test services and the calibration of test facilities.
(3) The Authority may, on the application of an approved test service provider, modify or waive any provision of the codes, standards of performance or specifications or any requirement in notices under paragraph (2), subject to such conditions as the Authority may impose.
[S 64/2013 wef 31/01/2013]
[S 641/2026 wef 21/09/2026]
[S 641/2026 wef 21/09/2026]

chapter.en: PART IIIA TESTING SERVICES

heading.en: Validity period of approval

text.en:
24F. Any approval granted by the Authority under regulation 24B(1) is valid for —
(a)where a period is specified by the Authority in the letter mentioned in regulation 24B(1), that period; and
(b)in any other case, the period starting on the date that the approval is granted and ending on the date that the approved test service provider discontinues as an approved test service provider under regulation 24J or the approval is cancelled under regulation 24K(1)(iii) or (1A).
[S 641/2026 wef 21/09/2026]

chapter.en: PART IIIA TESTING SERVICES

heading.en: Renewal of approval

text.en:
24G.—(1) Regulations 24A to 24F shall apply, with the necessary modifications and subject to this regulation, to an application to renew the term of approval for any test service provider.
(2) Any application to renew an approval for any test service provider must be —
(a)submitted to the Authority no later than 6 months before the date of expiry of the approval; and
(b)accompanied by the relevant renewal fee specified in the First Schedule, which fee is not refundable.
(3) If an application to renew an approval is submitted to the Authority less than 6 months before the date of expiry of the approval, the application must, in addition to the renewal fee, be accompanied by the relevant late application fee specified in the First Schedule, which fee is not refundable.
(4) If a requirement under this regulation is not complied with, the Authority may refuse to consider the application.
[S 64/2013 wef 31/01/2013]

chapter.en: PART IIIA TESTING SERVICES

heading.en: Regular investigation and determination of suitability and technical capability

text.en:
24H.—(1) The Authority may, from time to time, investigate —
(a)an approved test service provider; or
(b)any associate or business associate of the approved test service provider,
to determine whether the approved test service provider is suitable to continue to be an approved test service provider.
(2) For the purposes of the determination mentioned in paragraph (1), the Authority may have regard (but is not limited) to any matter in the Fourth Schedule as it applies to any person mentioned in that paragraph.
[S 641/2026 wef 21/09/2026]

chapter.en: PART IIIA TESTING SERVICES

heading.en: Ongoing monitoring of associates and others

text.en:
24I.—(1) The Authority may, from time to time, inquire into —
(a)any associate or business associate of an approved test service provider; or
(b)any person likely to become an associate of an approved test service provider.
[S 641/2026 wef 21/09/2026]
(2) In particular, the Authority must consider whether there is any information relating to any matter in the Fourth Schedule as it applies to any person mentioned in paragraph (1).
[S 641/2026 wef 21/09/2026]
(3) An approved test service provider shall notify the Authority in writing that a person is likely to become an associate of the approved test service provider as soon as practicable after the approved test service provider becomes aware of the likelihood.
(4) The Authority may, by notice in writing, require a person referred to in paragraph (1) —
(a)to provide the Authority, in accordance with directions in the notice, with such information relevant to the approved test service provider or the association or business association (as the case may be) of the person with the approved test service provider, or with such information as the Authority requires, as is specified in the notice;
[S 641/2026 wef 21/09/2026]
(b)to produce to the Authority, in accordance with the directions in the notice, such records relevant to the approved test service provider or that association or business association, or to matters specified by the Authority, as may be specified in the notice and to permit the Authority to examine the records, take extracts from them and make copies of them; or
[S 641/2026 wef 21/09/2026]
(c)to attend before the Authority for examination in relation to any matter relevant to the approved test service provider or that association or business association, or to matters specified by the Authority, and to answer questions relating to those matters.
[S 641/2026 wef 21/09/2026]
[S 641/2026 wef 21/09/2026]
(5) If records are produced under this regulation, the Authority may retain possession of the records for such period as may reasonably be necessary for inquiries to be carried out.
(6) At any reasonable time during the period for which records are retained, the Authority shall permit inspection of the records by a person who would be entitled to inspect them if they were not in the possession of the Authority.
(7) The Authority may —
(a)require any person mentioned in paragraph (1) who is an individual to consent to having his photograph, finger prints and palm prints taken; and
[S 641/2026 wef 21/09/2026]
(b)send a copy of such photograph, finger prints and palm prints, and any supporting documents to the Commissioner of Police.
(8) The Commissioner of Police or any police officer authorised by the Commissioner shall inquire into and report to the Authority on such matters concerning any person mentioned in paragraph (1) as the Authority requests.
[S 641/2026 wef 21/09/2026]
(9) If the Authority determines that —
(a)an associate of an approved test service provider has engaged or is engaging in conduct that, in the opinion of the Authority, is unacceptable for a person who is concerned in or associated with the management or operation of the business of the approved test service provider in providing testing services in relation to gaming equipment; or
(b)a business associate of an approved test service provider has engaged or is engaging in conduct that, in the opinion of the Authority, is unacceptable for a person who has a business association with the approved test service provider,
the Authority may give written notice to the associate or business associate mentioned in sub-paragraph (a) or (b) that the conduct is unacceptable.
[S 641/2026 wef 21/09/2026]
(10) If —
(a)the Authority, having regard to any matter referred to in paragraph (2), determines that —
(i)an associate of an approved test service provider is unsuitable to be concerned in or associated with the management or operation of the business of the approved test service provider in providing testing services in relation to gaming equipment; or
(ii)a business associate of an approved test service provider is unsuitable to have a business association with the approved test service provider; or
(b)the associate or business associate mentioned in paragraph (9)(a) or (b) continues with the conduct mentioned in paragraph (9),
the Authority may, by written notice, direct the approved test service provider to take all reasonable steps to terminate the association or business association (as the case may be) and the approved test service provider must comply with the direction within 14 days after receiving the notice or any longer period agreed with the Authority.
[S 641/2026 wef 21/09/2026]
[S 641/2026 wef 21/09/2026]

chapter.en: PART IIIA TESTING SERVICES

heading.en: Voluntary discontinuation as approved test service provider

text.en:
24J.—(1) An approved test service provider may, in writing to the Authority, request to discontinue as an approved test service provider.
(2) The Authority may refuse to allow the request under paragraph (1) if ––
(a)any action commenced by the Authority under regulation 24K, or any investigation which may result in such action, against the approved test service provider is pending; or
(b)any investigation by the Authority in respect of any gaming equipment tested by the approved test service provider is pending.
[S 64/2013 wef 31/01/2013]
[S 641/2026 wef 21/09/2026]

chapter.en: PART IIIA TESTING SERVICES

heading.en: Cancellation of approval, etc., in relation to approved test service provider

text.en:
24K.—(1) Where any approved test service provider —
(a)is, for specified reasons, considered by the Authority to be no longer suitable to continue to be an approved test service provider;
(aa)fails to comply with any condition imposed by the Authority under regulation 24B(1) or 28(1)(c);
[S 641/2026 wef 21/09/2026]
(b)fails to comply with regulation 24D(1) or (2), or a written notice issued under regulation 24D(4);
(ba)fails to comply with a written notice issued under regulation 24E(2);
[S 641/2026 wef 21/09/2026]
(c)is convicted of any offence under the Act or any regulations made thereunder;
(d)fails to provide testing services in accordance with the statement of independence provided by it to the Authority under regulation 24A(1)(d);
(e)fails to comply with regulation 24I(3) or (10);
[S 641/2026 wef 21/09/2026]
(f)fails to comply with the written notice of the Authority under regulation 26B(1); or
[S 641/2026 wef 21/09/2026]
(g)fails to comply with any condition of a waiver imposed by the Authority under regulation 28(1)(b) or 29(4)(b),
[S 641/2026 wef 21/09/2026]
the Authority may take any of the following actions:
(i)issue a letter of censure to the approved test service provider;
(ii)suspend its approval for the approved test service provider for a specified period not exceeding 6 months or suspend its approval for the approved test service provider to carry on testing services at such test facilities as may be specified by the Authority, for a specified period not exceeding 6 months;
(iii)cancel its approval for the approved test service provider or cancel its approval for the approved test service provider to carry on testing services at such test facilities as may be specified by the Authority.
(1A) The Authority may, in its discretion, cancel its approval of any approved test service provider which has had no business dealings with any approved manufacturer or casino operator for a continuous period of 3 years or more.
[S 641/2026 wef 21/09/2026]
(2) The Authority shall, before taking any action under paragraph (1) or (1A), serve on the approved test service provider a notice in writing giving the person an opportunity to show cause within 14 days, or such longer period as the Authority may allow on application by the approved test service provider, why action should not be taken under that paragraph.
[S 641/2026 wef 21/09/2026]
(3) The approved test service provider may, within the period allowed under paragraph (2), make submissions to the Authority as to why the action should not be taken and the Authority shall consider any submissions so made.
(4) The Authority may, if the approved test service provider fails to show cause within the period allowed by the Authority or fails to show sufficient cause, by notice in writing given to the approved test service provider, take such action in paragraph (1)(i), (ii) or (iii) against that person as the Authority sees fit.
(5) The suspension or cancellation of approval under this regulation shall take effect when the notice under paragraph (4) is given or on such later date as may be specified in the notice.
(6) While any approved test service provider is suspended under this regulation, it shall not, for the purposes of these Regulations, be regarded as an approved test service provider, as the case may be, during the period of its suspension.
[S 64/2013 wef 31/01/2013]
(7) The Authority may lift the suspension of its approval if it is satisfied that corrective action has been duly taken by the approved test service provider.
[S 641/2026 wef 21/09/2026]
[S 641/2026 wef 21/09/2026]

chapter.en: PART IV LINKED JACKPOT ARRANGEMENT

heading.en: Approval of linked jackpot arrangement

text.en:
25.—(1) An application for approval of the Authority for any linked jackpot arrangement under section 105(1) of the Act must contain ––
(a)a detailed description of the manner in which the linked jackpot arrangement operates, including the configured parameters for the linked jackpot arrangement;
[S 641/2026 wef 21/09/2026]
(b)a description of the linked jackpot arrangement, including all the gaming machines, gaming programs and linked jackpot equipment to be used in connection with the linked jackpot arrangement; and
[S 64/2013 wef 31/01/2013]
[S 641/2026 wef 21/09/2026]
(c)[Deleted by S 641/2026 wef 21/09/2026]
(d)[Deleted by S 641/2026 wef 21/09/2026]
(e)such other information as the Authority may require to consider the application.
(1A) The application under paragraph (1) must be accompanied by the appropriate application fee specified in the First Schedule, which fee is not refundable.
[S 64/2013 wef 31/01/2013]
(2) All linked jackpot equipment to be used in connection with a linked jackpot arrangement must be approved gaming equipment.
(2A) The Authority may refuse to consider an application under paragraph (1) if ––
(a)the application is incomplete; or
(b)the application fee is not paid.
[S 64/2013 wef 31/01/2013]
(3) The Authority may approve a linked jackpot arrangement, subject to such conditions as the Authority may impose.
[S 64/2013 wef 31/01/2013]

chapter.en: PART IV LINKED JACKPOT ARRANGEMENT

heading.en: Modification of linked jackpot arrangement

text.en:
25A.—(1) No person shall modify, or permit any modification of, an approved linked jackpot arrangement, unless the person has obtained the prior written approval of the Authority for the modification.
(2) Regulation 25 shall apply, with the necessary modifications, to an application for approval under paragraph (1) as it does to an application for approval under regulation 25(1).
(3) The Authority may waive the requirement to apply for approval under paragraph (1) if the Authority is of the opinion that the modification is minor having regard to bet limits, game integrity or security.
(4) Any person who contravenes paragraph (1) shall ––
(a)in the case of a casino operator, be liable to disciplinary action under section 54 of the Act;
[S 641/2026 wef 21/09/2026]
(aa)in the case of a licensed special employee, be liable to disciplinary action under section 93 of the Act; and
[S 641/2026 wef 21/09/2026]
(b)in the case of any other person, be guilty of an offence and shall be liable on conviction to a fine not exceeding $10,000 or to imprisonment for a term not exceeding 12 months or to both.
[S 64/2013 wef 31/01/2013]

chapter.en: PART IV LINKED JACKPOT ARRANGEMENT

heading.en: Decommissioning of linked jackpot arrangement

text.en:
25B.—(1) No person shall decommission any approved linked jackpot arrangement, unless it has obtained the prior written approval of the Authority for the decommission.
(2) An application for approval of the Authority for the decommission of the approved linked jackpot arrangement must contain ––
(a)a detailed description of the treatment of accumulated money upon termination of the linked jackpot arrangement;
[S 641/2026 wef 21/09/2026]
(b)a description of the linked jackpot arrangement, including all the gaming machines, gaming programs and linked jackpot equipment that had been used in connection with the linked jackpot arrangement; and
[S 641/2026 wef 21/09/2026]
(c)such other information as the Authority may require.
(3) The application under paragraph (2) must be accompanied by the appropriate application fee specified in the First Schedule, which fee is not refundable.
(4) The Authority may refuse to consider an application under paragraph (2) if ––
(a)the application is incomplete; or
(b)the application fee is not paid.
(5) The Authority may approve the decommission of any approved linked jackpot arrangement, subject to such conditions as the Authority may impose.
(6) Any person who contravenes paragraph (1) shall ––
(a)in the case of a casino operator, be liable to disciplinary action under section 54 of the Act;
[S 641/2026 wef 21/09/2026]
(aa)in the case of a licensed special employee, be liable to disciplinary action under section 93 of the Act; and
[S 641/2026 wef 21/09/2026]
(b)in the case of any other person, be guilty of an offence and shall be liable on conviction to a fine not exceeding $10,000 or to imprisonment for a term not exceeding 12 months or to both.
[S 64/2013 wef 31/01/2013]

chapter.en: PART IV LINKED JACKPOT ARRANGEMENT

heading.en: Prohibited linked jackpot arrangement

text.en:
26.—(1) For the purposes of section 105(2)(c) of the Act, a linked jackpot arrangement which is operated and administered by any person other than a casino operator is prohibited.
(2) A linked jackpot arrangement is operated and administered by a person if that person has control over the operation, maintenance or use of the linked jackpot equipment used in connection with the linked jackpot arrangement.

chapter.en: PART IVA PROVISIONS AS TO COSTS

heading.en: Costs of investigation of applications to be borne by applicant

text.en:
26A.—(1) The costs of investigation of an application by any relevant person shall be borne by the applicant or each applicant in the group of applicants (in the case of a consolidated application, if applicable).
(2) The Authority may give a written notice to the applicant or group of applicants of the estimated costs of investigation and require the applicant or group of applicants to pay such estimated costs to the Authority within such period as may be specified in the notice.
(3) At the conclusion of the investigation into the application or if the application is withdrawn, the Authority shall certify the actual costs of investigation of the application, and shall ––
(a)where the actual costs of investigation are lower than the amount paid under paragraph (2), refund the excess without interest to the person who paid the estimated costs; or
(b)where the actual costs of investigation are higher than the amount paid under paragraph (2), by a written notice, require the person to reimburse the Authority the excess within such period as may be specified in the notice.
(4) The certificate of the Authority stating the actual costs of the investigation under paragraph (3) shall be conclusive evidence of such amount.
(5) In this regulation, “relevant person” means any person who submits an application to be an approved manufacturer or approved test service provider.
[S 641/2026 wef 21/09/2026]

chapter.en: PART IVA PROVISIONS AS TO COSTS

heading.en: Costs of investigation of suitability to be borne by approved manufacturer or approved test service provider

text.en:
26B.—(1) For the purpose of meeting any costs arising out of any investigation in connection with the continuing suitability of any approved manufacturer or approved test service provider, the Authority may, from time to time, give a written notice to the approved manufacturer or approved test service provider (as the case may be) to pay such estimated costs to the Authority within such period of time as may be specified in the notice.
[S 641/2026 wef 21/09/2026]
(2) Regulation 26A(3) and (4) shall apply, with the necessary modifications and subject to this regulation, to any costs of investigation of suitability under paragraph (1) as it does to the costs of investigation of application under regulation 26A(1).
[S 64/2013 wef 31/01/2013]
[S 641/2026 wef 21/09/2026]

chapter.en: PART V GENERAL

heading.en: Power of inspector to stop casino gambling, etc., until corrective action taken

text.en:
27.—(1) Without prejudice to the generality of section 15(1) of the Act, where an inspector knows or reasonably suspects that any gaming equipment (including any gaming machine or gaming program) in a casino —
(a)being a gaming machine or gaming program ––
(i)was acquired from a manufacturer or supplier of gaming machines or gaming programs which was not an approved manufacturer or authorised supplier at the time of its acquisition;
[S 64/2013 wef 31/01/2013]
[S 641/2026 wef 21/09/2026]
(ii)is not of a class of gaming machines or gaming programs approved by the Authority; or
[S 64/2013 wef 31/01/2013]
[S 641/2026 wef 21/09/2026]
(iii)approval of which, or any component thereof approval of which, has been revoked under regulation 16;
[S 64/2013 wef 31/01/2013]
[S 641/2026 wef 21/09/2026]
[S 641/2026 wef 21/09/2026]
(b)being gaming equipment for which approval is required under regulation 19, is not approved gaming equipment;
(ba)being gaming equipment, which approval or any component thereof has been revoked under regulation 23;
[S 64/2013 wef 31/01/2013]
(c)has been modified without the prior written approval or waiver of the Authority under regulation 15 or 22; or
[S 64/2013 wef 31/01/2013]
(d)has failed to function in the manner in which it was designed and programmed to function or in accordance with these Regulations, the technical standards or any other requirements in notices given by the Authority in relation to that gaming equipment or class of gaming equipment,
the inspector may ––
(A)stop the use of, or stop any casino gambling that uses, the gaming equipment, for such time as may be required to investigate the matter;
[S 64/2013 wef 31/01/2013]
[S 641/2026 wef 21/09/2026]
(B)require the casino operator to take such corrective action as may be necessary to ensure that the gaming equipment complies with these Regulations; or
[S 64/2013 wef 31/01/2013]
(C)if necessary for the purpose of investigating any suspected contravention of any provision of the Act or regulations made thereunder, seize the gaming equipment or any part thereof.
[S 64/2013 wef 31/01/2013]
[S 641/2026 wef 21/09/2026]
(2) Where the Authority is of the opinion that the manufacturing process of the manufacturer of gaming equipment is inconsistent with the representations made by it in any application for approval of that gaming equipment, the Authority may stop the use of any gaming equipment or any component thereof provided by that manufacturer.
[S 64/2013 wef 31/01/2013]
[S 641/2026 wef 21/09/2026]

chapter.en: PART V GENERAL

heading.en: Variation, etc., of conditions by Authority

text.en:
28.—(1) The Authority may at its discretion —
(a)vary or revoke any condition imposed by the Authority under these Regulations (called in this regulation Condition X);
(b)waive Condition X, subject to any condition that the Authority may impose; or
(c)impose a new condition in addition to Condition X.
(2) The Authority must not vary, revoke or waive, or impose a new condition in addition to, Condition X, unless the Authority has first served on the person on whom Condition X has been imposed a written notice, giving the person an opportunity to show cause within a specified period why Condition X should not be varied, revoked or waived, or why a new condition should not be imposed.
(3) After considering any submissions made by the person mentioned in paragraph (2), the Authority may, by written notice given to the person, vary, revoke or waive Condition X, or impose the new condition.
(4) The variation, revocation, waiver or imposition mentioned in paragraph (3) takes effect when the notice is given or on any later date specified in the notice.
[S 641/2026 wef 21/09/2026]

chapter.en: PART V GENERAL

heading.en: Application to vary, revoke or waive conditions

text.en:
29.—(1) Any person on whom any condition has been imposed by the Authority under these Regulations (called in this regulation Condition X) may apply to the Authority to vary, revoke or waive Condition X.
(2) An application under paragraph (1) must be —
(a)submitted to the Authority in the form and manner specified by the Authority; and
(b)accompanied by any information or document that the Authority may require to decide on the application.
(3) The Authority may refuse to consider an application under paragraph (1) if the application is ––
(a)incomplete; or
(b)not submitted in the form or manner, or accompanied by the information or document, mentioned in paragraph (2)(a) or (b).
(4) After considering the application mentioned in paragraph (1), the Authority may, by written notice given to the applicant —
(a)vary or revoke Condition X; or
(b)waive Condition X, subject to any condition that the Authority may impose.
(5) The variation, revocation or waiver mentioned in paragraph (4)(a) or (b) takes effect when the notice is given or on any later date specified in the notice.
(6) To avoid doubt, Condition X includes any condition imposed as a condition of a waiver under paragraph (4)(b).
[S 641/2026 wef 21/09/2026]
